children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to ask you a few questions about your child or children.

**First, let me ask about the child's age:**

How old is your child? This helps determine the initial eligibility criteria:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (subject to other conditions)
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over are not eligible

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have multiple children you're asking about, let me know their ages too.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you with Alex's eligibility.

Since Alex is 15 years old (under 16), that's a good start. Let me continue with the assessment by checking the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check Alex's work status:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is an important requirement - children working 24 or more hours per week generally aren't eligible for Child Benefit unless they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're just focused on school right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex isn't working, that's another requirement met. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking if Alex is receiving benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in their own name. Most 15-year-olds don't receive these benefits, but I need to confirm.

Does Alex receive any benefits in their own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship program?**

This includes:
- Apprenticeships in England (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, or Degree Apprenticeships)
- Modern Apprenticeships in Scotland
- Apprenticeships in Wales (except Foundation level, which are approved)

Since Alex is 15 and focused on school, I assume they're not in an apprenticeship, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship. They're just at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex meets all the child-related criteria so far. Now let me check the requirements about you as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status:

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common scenario)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively looking for work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support your family
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Do any of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Living in Manchester means you meet the UK residency requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You meet this requirement if ANY of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common scenario)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards their care - this includes food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds the Child Benefit payment

Do any of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're meeting all the requirements so far. Let me check the next criterion.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time. For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) claiming Child Benefit for them?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other relative) claiming it?

If someone else is claiming but you've all agreed that you should be the one to claim instead, that's fine - we can proceed. But if there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC would need to make that decision.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following best describes Alex's current living situation?**

- Alex is in hospital
- Alex is in local authority care
- Alex is fostered
- **Alex is living normally at home with you** (I expect this is the case based on what you've told me)

Please confirm which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex is fostered. I'm fostering them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that! Since you're fostering Alex, I need to check a specific requirement about the fostering arrangement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Important question about the fostering arrangement:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council paying you a fostering allowance or contributing to Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?

You can only claim Child Benefit for a fostered child if the local council is NOT paying for their accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - I don't get anything from the council to foster them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You've already confirmed that the council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance. Let me move to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me now provide you with the final eligibility determination.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You're Eligible!

**You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - At 15 years old, Alex is under 16  
✅ **Alex's circumstances** - Not working, not receiving benefits, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✅ **Your residency** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **Your responsibility** - You live with and care for Alex  
✅ **No competing claims** - Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✅ **Fostering arrangement** - Importantly, the local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance, which means you can claim Child Benefit even though you're fostering

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earn over £60,000, you may need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return (though you can still claim)
5. **Payments** - You'll receive payments every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can apply here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
